# OrangeCrab r0.2.1 outline reproduction

Source: [official OrangeCrab hardware](https://github.com/orangecrab-fpga/orangecrab-hardware/tree/c511d569fe2af39467041f888bc231020f40c6ac/hardware/orangecrab_r0.2.1), an ECP5 FPGA with x16 DDR3L on six copper layers. Upstream licences, the source revision, source SHA-256 and exact removed IDs are retained beside the captures.

`original.circuit.json` preserves all 163 PCB components, 441 vias, pad geometry, placement and authored copper. `byte0.srj.json` is the unchanged native routing capture for eleven byte-zero signals, with 1,430 obstacles and 996 fixed wire runs. The PCB view removes exactly 19 named trace records and 22 named vias. Regression tests pin both capture hashes, independently name every removed element, and compare every unrelated element against the original. The six-layer stack, routing layers, 0.089 mm width/gap and captured 1 mm bus/pair length limits remain unchanged. These captured routing limits are not an independent signal-integrity qualification.

J1 and J2 are intentionally castellated Feather headers. Each pin has an inner through-hole and an edge drill joined by copper. Their 56 original 1 mm drills have 1.4 mm spacing within each pin and 2.54 mm pitch between pins. Edge-drill centers sit 0.13 mm outside the routed board boundary. This is source geometry that becomes a milled edge contact; it must not be moved, hidden or deduplicated to make a preview cleaner.

Run `bun test tests/repros`. This repro asserts the existing `unsupported_outline` failure without exporting failed or unrouted images. A fully routed rectangular synthetic positive control supplies its before/after SVG panels; production behavior is unchanged in a repro PR. The same completed image in both panels is intentional and does not depict the failing real board. The stacked outline fix adds a completely routed synthetic concave control, validated before its `toMatchPcbSnapshot` call. The later offset-pair and pair-only target issues have separate repro/fix PRs and synthetic fixtures.

Accepting this real outline, completing a small synthetic control, and completing the complete OrangeCrab DDR lane are distinct results. The full real lane still has native-approach failures. Original pours require native refill and DRC after a successful reroute. No full DDR completion, timing closure, impedance verification or hardware validation is claimed.
